newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Dublin prison siege enters third day.
newsitem.headline: Dublin prison siege enters third day.

text.p: Prison officials held talks for the third day on Monday to try to free four warders held hostage by six prisoners armed with metal bars and a blood-filled syringe inside Dublin's Mountjoy prison.

Food was sent to the group, barricaded inside a recreation hall in the North Dublin prison since Saturday night. The prisoners are protesting about alleged mistreatment and demanding transfer to another jail.

The heroin substitute physeptone was also provided for the prisoners -- two are reported to be addicted to the drug, which has become a major earner for the gangland underworld and the scourge of low-income housing estates.

The use of the blood-filled syringe in the hostage-taking was a clear threat to infect a hostage with AIDS. There are several victims of the illness in the prison as well as people suffering from the HIV virus which causes it, officials said.

One of the hostage-takers is Paul Ward, on remand in connection with the murder last year of investigative reporter Veronica Guerin, whose death was thought to have been ordered by a drug baron she was writing about.
Ward faces charges of conspiracy in connection with Guerin's death and a drug offence.
The other prisoners are serving terms of between five and 10 years jail for violent crimes including manslaughter, kidnapping and assault.
The Department of Justice said the men's complaints would be investigated.
